title: Deployment dashboard charts
summary: Workspace / Deployments as charts on one aggregate: delivery figures, a tile map of projects by environments (drift, last run, health, waiting approvals, not set up, missing backup), a release flow with a virtualised card list, a deploy timeline with a time brush, and an opt-in 3D deploy landscape; filters in the link, cross-filter, keyboard and table alternatives. Measured on 40 projects, 4 environments, 6 tenants, 2,000 runs and 5,000 cards: uPlot plus small own forms (29.9 kB gzip) recommended over Apache ECharts (220.7 kB) and Chart.js with plugins (82.1 kB), in line with the live structure canvas Dossier; 3D on Canvas 2D (2.8 kB) instead of three.js (131.8 kB) or echarts-gl. Persona assessments as validated view specifications on top of facts. Ten decisions, eight slices, first the overview and the release flow on real data with the aggregation API and budget tests.

coveredElsewhere.slice: Instance deploy records, live release, cards integrated but not live
Dashboard data: the instance's Production in /api/deploy/matrix and /api/deploy/cards, projects without environments, delivery lanes for watched projects
Structure facts, data locations with backup coverage, facts for warnings, live deltas
Topology of hosts, containers and services as the live structure canvas; canvas renderer and chart library for the hosting area
Persona scheduling, admission, budget ledger, items and importance
Persona view specifications for the structure canvas, sharing the occurrence with DDC-6

visualStack.chartLibrary: uPlot (D1 A, same as D2 A of docs/live-structure-canvas/)
visualStack.ownForms: tile map and sparklines on Canvas 2D, release flow as SVG

openDecisions.title: Chart framework
openDecisions.question: Which chart framework draws the deployment dashboard and, with it, every chart of the hosting area?

options.A: uPlot for time charts plus small own forms on Canvas 2D and SVG (the D2 recommendation of the live structure canvas Dossier)
options.C: Chart.js 4 with the matrix, sankey and zoom plugins

openDecisions.rationale: Smallest lazy chunk and fastest filter change in the prototype, one library for the Studio as the structure canvas Dossier already recommends; ECharts stays the measured fallback when a form is needed that is not worth building.

openDecisions.title: Angular wrapper
openDecisions.question: How do Angular components host a chart?

options.A: A thin own chart host: signal inputs, one instance reused, ResizeObserver, dispose on destroy, loaded with a dynamic import
options.B: A wrapper library of the chosen framework
options.C: No wrapper, each view talks to the library

openDecisions.rationale: A small component, no second dependency to keep in step with Angular and the library, and the same host serves uPlot and the own forms.

openDecisions.title: Views first
openDecisions.question: Which views are built first?

options.A: Overview and release flow, then the timeline, then the delivery figures

openDecisions.rationale: Overview and flow replace the table and the long card column the owner criticised; they need no library, so the first slice proves data, filters and budget.

openDecisions.title: 3D
openDecisions.question: Is there a 3D view, and with which renderer?

options.A: Yes, opt-in: the deploy landscape drawn with Canvas 2D, loaded when opened; default views stay 2D

openDecisions.rationale: The third axis carries the run count and the view flattens into its 2D heat map; 2.4 kB gzip instead of a second renderer of more than 100 kB, in line with one canvas renderer for the Studio.

openDecisions.title: Landing view
openDecisions.question: What does Workspace / Deployments open with?

options.A: Delivery figures and the overview tile map, release flow and timeline below on the same page
options.C: Today's table, charts on a second tab

openDecisions.rationale: Answers what is live where and what is behind before any scrolling; a persona may reorder the views for its reader (D9).

openDecisions.title: Topology
openDecisions.question: Where does the topology of hosts, containers and services live?

options.A: In Operations, as the live structure canvas; the deployment page links to it with the project and environment as filter
options.B: As a tab of the deployment page

openDecisions.rationale: One drawing of the machines; the canvas has its own concept (AGT-3955) and renderer, and two copies would drift apart.

openDecisions.title: Roles that assess
openDecisions.question: Which personas assess the deployment views?

options.A: Operations warden and reliability engineer, both already in the catalogue

openDecisions.rationale: Backups, credentials and goals belong to the warden, failure clusters and flow to the reliability engineer; same choice as the structure canvas, so one occurrence can serve both views.

openDecisions.title: Refresh cadence
openDecisions.question: When do the personas reassess the deployment views?

options.A: On relevant fact changes, coalesced, plus a check every 12 hours that calls the model only when the facts digest changed

openDecisions.rationale: Fresh after a deploy or a failure, no model call when nothing changed, and inside the weekly allowance of each persona.

openDecisions.title: How much the model composes
openDecisions.question: How much of the deployment page may be LLM-composed?

options.B: Assessment on top of facts: order of views, emphasised figures and tiles, callouts, goals and a judgement, as a validated view specification
options.C: The model also chooses chart types, grouping and scales

openDecisions.rationale: Facts, scales and colours stay deterministic and comparable from day to day; the persona says what matters and what to do next, and an invalid answer falls back to the facts.

openDecisions.title: Aggregation API
openDecisions.question: How do the views get their data?

options.A: One aggregate, GET /api/deploy/dashboard, for all views, plus a paged card list
options.C: Keep joining per-project endpoints in the browser

openDecisions.rationale: One request and one consistent as-of for every view instead of 1 + N requests; filters change the query, not the number of calls.

implementationTasks.title: Deployment overview and release flow on the dashboard aggregate

# Deployment overview and release flow on the dashboard aggregate

Source: `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/index.html` (AGT-3950). Read AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/start/README.md first. Use the recommendation of each decision named below unless the Dossier records another choice, and state which option you implemented. Git ownership stays with the platform. This is one bounded slice.

## Deliver
1. Backend: `GET /api/deploy/dashboard?group=&project=&environment=&tenant=&from=&to=&outcome=` as specified in `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/stack.html`, section Aggregation, built in the deploy feature from the existing projections (`DeployMatrixResponse`, `CardDeploymentView`, delivery columns, `Deployment`, instance deploy records of AGT-3879 and AGT-3949). Parts for this slice: `projects`, `environments`, `tiles` (set up or not, live and newest release, `releasesBehind`, last run with state and failed step, health, approvals waiting, per tenant), `flow` (nodes, links, `waitingByProject`). 10-second cache like `/api/environment/flow`; a task hub event `deployDashboardChanged`, at most one a second.
2. Frontend, in `frontend/src/app/features/deployments/`: a lazy `deployment-dashboard-charts` chunk loaded with a dynamic import from the existing dashboard component; a chart host component (D2 A: signal inputs, one instance reused, `ResizeObserver`, dispose on destroy); the overview tile map (port `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/src/charts.js`, `tileMap`) and the release flow (`flowView`) on Studio tokens in both themes; text alternative as a table; keyboard as in the prototype.
3. Filters project group, project, environment and tenant as state of the route (`#/workspace/deployments?...`), restored from a pasted link; clicking a tile or a flow state filters the other view; active filters as removable chips.
4. The landing view follows D5; the plain table stays reachable as the text alternative. Projects without environments stay visible as not set up.
5. No per-project request on this page any more: the per-project `delivery-lanes` polling of the dashboard is removed.

## Acceptance
- Backend tests: the aggregate for a fixture of 40 projects, 4 environments, 6 tenants and 5,000 cards equals the per-project projections; projects without environments are in `tiles` as not set up; the instance's Production is present.
- Playwright with the dev backend fixture: the page issues exactly one dashboard request on load and one per filter change; screenshots of overview and flow in light and dark at 1440 and 390 px in the results folder.
- Budget tests: build stats show the initial bundle unchanged against develop and the new lazy chunk at most 12 kB gzip; on the 40-project fixture the first chart is painted within 300 ms after the response and a filter change within 100 ms (performance marks read by Playwright, median of 5).
- A pasted link restores the filters; every tile is reachable by keyboard and the table alternative lists the same values.

Source: `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/index.html` (AGT-3950). Read AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/start/README.md first. Use the recommendation of each decision named below unless the Dossier records another choice, and state which option you implemented. Git ownership stays with the platform. ## Deliver
1. Backend: `GET /api/deploy/dashboard/cards?stage=&offset=&limit=` with the dashboard filters, newest first, limit at most 200, total count in the response.
2. Frontend: clicking a state of the release flow opens the card list under it; fixed row height, only the visible window plus a small buffer in the DOM (own windowing as in `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/src/app.js`, `drawCards`, or `@angular/cdk/scrolling` if it does not grow the initial bundle); rows link to the card; key, project, state, integrated date, waiting time or lead time.

- With 5,000 cards in a state the list holds fewer than 60 row elements while scrolling (asserted in a Playwright test).
- Pages are requested as the window moves, at most one request in flight; the count line states rows shown and total.
- Keyboard: the list is reachable by Tab, scrolls with the arrow keys and each visible row link can be focused.

# Deploy timeline with time brush on uPlot

Source: `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/index.html` (AGT-3950). Read AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/start/README.md first. ## Deliver

Source: `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/index.html` (AGT-3950). Read AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/start/README.md first. ## Deliver
1. Schema `deploy-view-spec/v1` and validator from `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/src/spec.js` and `docs/deployment-dashboard-charts/schema/`, server-side and in the client; anything invalid is not drawn and the reasons are shown.
